Verbos com -ся: a ação volta para quem f: Verbs with -ся: the action comes back to the doer
Alguns verbos terminam em -ся, como «про: Some verbs end in -ся, such as «просыпаться» (to wake up) and «умываться» (to wash oneself). The action comes back to the person who does it, like "to get oneself up". English often leaves this out ("I wash", "I wake up"), or uses "myself", but Russian marks it on the verb. Conjugate normally and add -сь if the form ends in a vowel (я просыпаюсь, вы просыпаетесь) or -ся if it ends in a consonant (он просыпается, они просыпаются). «Вставать» (to get up) follows the same pattern without -ся: я встаю.
I get up at seven o'clock.
We have lunch in a café.

Já vimos «Где?» (onde): «в» + preposicio: We have already seen «Где?» (where): «в» + prepositional («в магазине»). To ask «Куда?» (where to, with movement), use the ACCUSATIVE: «Я иду в магазин», «Я еду на работу». In short: standing still → prepositional; moving → accusative. For "home" there is a word of its own, with no preposition: «домой» (going home); "at home" is «дома». The verbs «идти» (on foot) and «ехать» (by bus, car or train) are irregular: learn the forms.
em português usamos «à loja» para o movi: in English we say "in the shop" for place and "to the shop" for movement. Russian keeps the same preposition and changes the ending of the word.
